data.gender_notes: Shaulor is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Shaulor is derived from the Hebrew name Shaul (שָׁאול), which means 'asked of God'. In the Bible, Shaul (Saul) was the first king of Israel, chosen by God and anointed by the prophet Samuel. Shaul's story is one of faith, obedience, and transformation. The name Shaulor carries the meaning “Asked of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Shaulor usually hope their child will grow to embody asked of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Shaulor belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Asked of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shaulor total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: שאולור
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם שאולור מקורו בשם העברי שאול, שפירושו 'נשאל מאלוהים' או 'שאול מן האל'. השם שאול היה שמו של מלך ישראל הראשון, שאול בן קיש, אשר מוזכר בספר שמואל. השם גם מתקשר לנביא שאול, שהיה אחד מתלמידי ישוע. מבחינה רוחנית, השם שאולור מייצג קשר ישיר עם האל ומבטא בקשה או תחינה אלוהית.

in_greek.name: Σαουλόρ
in_greek.long_meaning: Τὸ όνομα Σαουλόρ προέρχεται από το εβραϊκό όνομα Σαούλ (Saul), που σημαίνει 'αἰτητός παρὰ θεοῦ' ή 'κληθείς από τον Θεό'. Στο Καινὴ Διαθήκη, ο Σαούλ αναφέρεται ως ο πρώτος βασιλιάς του Ισραήλ και ως ένας από τους μαθητές του Ιησού Χριστού. Το όνομα Σαουλόρ έχει έντονη πνευματική σημασία, συμβολίζοντας τη σχέση μεταξύ του ανθρώπου και του Θεού.

in_latin.name: Shaulor
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Shaulor derivatur ex nomine hebraico Saul, quod significat 'Dei eximius' vel 'a Deo petitur'. In scripturis sacris, Saul fuit primus rex Israelis et unus ex discipulis Jesu Christi. Spiritualiter, nomen Shaulor repraesentat nexum directum cum Deo et precum instantiam.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shaulor is a modern variation of the traditional Hebrew name Shaul, but it lacks any cultural significance as it is not a name in common usage in Jewish or Christian communities. Nevertheless, the historical figure of King Saul has had a significant cultural impact on Western civilization. As the first monarch of Israel, Saul's reign was a turning point in the history of the Jewish people and paved the way for the development of a centralized monarchy in the ancient Near East. Additionally, numerous works of literature, music, and visual art have been inspired by the story of Saul and his reign.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Shaulor holds deep spiritual significance as it is derived from the Hebrew word shaul, which means 'asked of God'. In the Bible, Saul's story is a testament to the idea that even those who may not initially possess the qualities required to lead can be chosen and anointed by God to fulfill an important role. Saul's story also illustrates the themes of obedience, faithfulness, and transformation. Ultimately, the name Shaulor serves as a reminder that regardless of our background or perceived shortcomings, we all have the potential to be vessels of God's will and to make a positive impact on the world around us.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shaul means "asked" or "questioned" in Hebrew. The name Shaul in the Bible belongs to Saul, the first king of Israel. In a spiritual sense, the name can represent the seeking soul, the one who questions and searches for truth and meaning in life. The name Shaulor could symbolize the deep inner yearning and restlessness of the human spirit, the longing for answers and understanding that drives us forward on our spiritual journey.

During the Middle Ages, Christians adopted the practice of naming their children after saints, and some mothers gave their daughters the name Shaulor, which derived from the Latin word for 'harvest' and the Greek goddess Selene.
